answer: Size the bond to the prize, not to the identity. Capturing a decision worth V requires the deciding quorum to collectively escrow at least V in a slashable vault, forfeited if their verdict is later overturned. Splitting into a thousand sybils buys no discount: the bond tracks the outcome's value, so a cheap clone army must still post the full V and lose it when caught. The raid stalls at the wharf because seizing the verdict costs more than the verdict pays, and a forged quill only ever signs a losing trade.
